content: Indication-specific dosing for Atlantic yam, barbasco, China root, and wild yam in combination includes detailed information on frequency-based adverse effects, comprehensive drug interactions, contraindications, pregnancy and lactation guidelines, and cost considerations. Oral doses of these substances are used for various conditions, including estrogen replacement therapy, painful menstruation (dysmenorrhea), libido enhancement, breast enlargement, diverticulosis, gallbladder colic, osteoporosis, postmenopausal vaginal dryness, premenstrual syndrome, and rheumatoid arthritis. However, when applied topically, these substances appear to be no more effective than a placebo in alleviating vasomotor symptoms. When taken orally, they are possibly ineffective, and further studies are required to confirm their efficacy. Adverse effects may include vomiting. These substances are contraindicated in individuals with hormone-sensitive conditions such as breast, ovarian, or uterine cancer, endometriosis, and uterine fibroids. Regarding pregnancy, there is no specific category assigned (N/A), and lactation safety is also not established (N/A). However, in general, these substances are considered acceptable (Category A), as controlled studies in pregnant women have shown no evidence of fetal risk.
